source: Library of Congress, Sanborn Fire Insurance Map, St. Louis Vol. 12 (1938, revised to 1950), sheet 74, image 04858_12_1950-0074
labeled_by: AI-assisted draft from the 1938 key: each site compared with the 1950 scan side by side, 2026-10-19
scope: Industrial, fuel, tank and vehicle-service uses, plus stores and warehouses for paint, hardware or building materials, plus every G.T. symbol. Excludes dwellings, general stores and flats, offices, clinics, banks, post offices, general/grocery/furniture/merchandise storage, and auto houses (A) with no other use. Groups (a field of tanks) are one entry.

definitions.gasoline_tank_count: Number of tanks the map labels as gasoline: G.T. / G.T.S. symbols, 'GASOL. STGE. TKS.', or a labeled gasoline tank. 0 means none drawn.
definitions.other_tanks: Tanks that are not labeled gasoline (water, grain, iron, fuel oil, etc.).
definitions.map_notes: Only what is printed on the sheet.
definitions.interpretation: Inference, not a map fact; never scored.

sheet_layout: Laclede Gas coke & by-products plant fills the left two-thirds, between the River Des Peres (left) and E Catalan; rail yard and coal/coke piles to the south by the Mississippi. Dwellings on Reilly Av and E Espenschied at top right. Scale 100 ft to an inch.
plant_note: Watchman, central station service. Heat: steam. Power: steam & electric. Fuel: coal, coke & gas. Water from the Mississippi River (Worthington centrifugal pump, 1,500 gpm).
false_positive_test: No G.T. symbols on this sheet. GASOMETER and GAS PRODUCER refer to manufactured (coal) gas, not gasoline; a model that counts them as gasoline tanks is wrong.
out_of_scope_seen: Dwellings and auto houses on Reilly Av and E Espenschied
Small plant supply, rod and pipe sheds
Plant office near the coke pile (638)
